correctness.rationale: With exact unpivoted QR, first block direction q1=(X,epsilon Y)/sqrt(X^2+epsilon^2Y^2) for independent real Gaussians X,Y (X=0 null event). Put s=epsilon^2Y^2/(X^2+epsilon^2Y^2); row energy squares are 1-(1-epsilon^2)s and epsilon^2+(1-epsilon^2)s, summing 1+epsilon^2. Algorithm 3.2 discards a smaller row iff its squared energy is <tau^2 on exact-zero residual. With u=(tau^2-epsilon^2)/(1-epsilon^2), and 0<u<1/2 for epsilon<(2c^2-1)^-1/2, both retained exactly when u<=s<=1-u (ties probability zero). Ratio Y/X is standard Cauchy, giving the difference of two arctangent probabilities. Limit as epsilon->0 is (2/pi) arctan(1/sqrt(c^2-1)). Eckart--Young singular values 1,epsilon show optimal residual epsilon<tau for rank1, while rank0 fails tau<||A||. Actual Frobenius look-ahead at first test rejects with probability at most 1-e^(-c^2 epsilon^2); with a complete rank-two block the next residual is zero and conditional probability differs from the unconditional Cauchy law by at most this rejection probability. Numerically evaluated exact formula at c=sqrt2,epsilon=0.005: 0.499976126 vs limiting 0.5; this is corroboration only. The publisher code explicitly sorts row norms and discards until strict test fails.

value.rationale: Motivated exact diagnosis of the efficiency criterion introduced for a current adaptive matrix-free algorithm: a natural rank-two spectrum and Gaussian sketch have a limiting one-half chance of returning two rows despite rank-one optimality. The finite exact distribution, limiting threshold law and controlled look-ahead make a nontrivial reproducible boundary to a claimed near-minimal-rank property; routine singular-value optimality alone does not yield this sensitivity.

final_claim: For A_epsilon=diag(1,epsilon,0,0), two-column Gaussian sketches with unpivoted QR, absolute Frobenius threshold tau=c epsilon (c>1 and epsilon sufficiently small), the optimal rank is one but Smith--Do--Chen Frobenius row-pruning returns two retained rows with exact finite-epsilon Cauchy-angle probability, converging to (2/pi) arctan[1/sqrt(c^2-1)]. At c=sqrt2 the limit is 1/2. The actual initial-lookahead rejection has probability <=1-exp(-c^2 epsilon^2), so the full matrix-free method has the same limit on the successful first block.
limitations: Real 4x4 diagonal rank-two input, unpivoted two-column real Gaussian sketch, absolute tolerance and successful first-block look-ahead in exact arithmetic only.
No claim about general rank efficiency or finite-precision effects; event conditioning handled by vanishing first-rejection bound, not by unjustified independence.
